(Photo by Alexis JUMEAU / POOL / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Estonia is investigating possible Russian involvement in a suspected arson attack on a defense contractor whose unmanned military systems are deployed in Ukraine, Prime Minister Kristen Michal said Tuesday. A building used by Milrem Robotics on Betooni Street in Tallinn caught fire overnight into Saturday. Preliminary evidence suggests the blaze may have been deliberately set, according to Estonia’s public broadcaster ERR. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . “The suspects have been identified,” Michal wrote on X, adding that one line of investigation concerns “a possible act of sabotage and the involvement of Russia.” Estonian Prosecutor General Astrid Asi said investigators had identified suspects based on evidence gathered by the Internal Security Service and the North Prefecture. Prosecutors have asked a court to detain them while authorities examine possible motives, including sabotage. Advertisement The investigation remains at an early stage and Estonian authorities have not established Russian responsibility. The Russian Embassy in Tallinn did not immediately respond to Reuters’ request for comment. Moscow has repeatedly denied Western accusations that it has organized sabotage and other covert attacks in Europe. Michal said Estonia was treating the incident particularly seriously because it targeted the country’s defense industry . “Attempts to intimidate us or undermine our security will not succeed,” he said, according to Reuters. “We will protect our people and our companies by any means necessary.” Other Topics of Interest Lavrov Threatens UK With ‘Consequences’ Over Ukraine War Russia’s foreign minister escalates Moscow’s warning to London after the Kremlin accused Britain of enabling Ukrainian deep strikes. Milrem Robotics develops military robotics and autonomous systems, including its THeMIS unmanned ground vehicle. The company says the platform has been operating in Ukraine since 2022 for missions including logistics, casualty evacuation and route clearance. In June, Milrem and Dutch company VDL Defentec began handing over the first vehicles from a new production line established to support a Netherlands-funded delivery of more than 100 THeMIS systems to Ukraine. Advertisement The suspected arson comes amid heightened concern across NATO’s eastern flank over Russian sabotage and hybrid operations. Poland and the Baltic states have recently strengthened protection around critical infrastructure, while officials have warned that Moscow could seek to stage attacks designed to undermine support for Ukraine.
